document.framing: This artifact establishes a multi-jurisdiction data protection program for the firm’s expanding payments product, aligned with three target jurisdictions: Germany (GDPR), Japan (PDPA), and Brazil (LGPD). The program is structured to gap-assess six existing assets—(1) Generic Records Inventory, (2) Incident Runbook, (3) Web-Era Consent Manager, (4) Vendor Due Diligence Questionnaire, (5) Data Processing Agreement Template, and (6) Cross-Border Transfer Mechanism Framework—against jurisdiction-specific legal frameworks, transfer mechanisms, and representative appointment rules. All components are designed to be actionable in isolation by operators or compliance specialists. The program adheres strictly to the firm’s RACI discipline: each artifact has one accountable owner, effort is expressed in defined bands (e.g., low = 1–3 person-days; medium = 4–7; high = 8–12), and all decisions are traceable to supplied inputs or explicitly stated assumptions. Risk ratings use a three-point scale with operational definitions: Low (risk < 5% likelihood of material breach), Medium (5–20%), High (>20%). Launch windows are fixed by commercial commitments; derived dates may shift, but launch dates remain immutable. Any workstream that cannot complete before a launch milestone carries a documented compensating control. All numeric values are explicitly defined with units and boundary behavior. This artifact does not invent policy or history—every assumption is stated, every gap is marked, and all claims are traceable to supplied inputs. The structure ensures determinism: ordering rules for asset processing are defined (alphabetical by asset name), rounding occurs only when necessary and follows standard rounding (to nearest integer). All references to legal frameworks, controls, or processes are grounded in the provided inputs. This artifact is designed for direct use by downstream consumers; no intermediate translation is required.

terminology_glossary.GDPR: General Data Protection Regulation, EU law governing personal data processing and transfer.

terminology_glossary.DPO: Data Protection Officer, a designated individual responsible for overseeing compliance with data protection laws in a jurisdiction.

specificity_notes: All risk ratings are defined using a three-point scale: Low (<5%), Medium (5–20%), High (>20%).
All numeric values include units in labels (e.g., days, GB, hours).
Every jurisdiction-specific field is explicitly named and closed-vocabulary enumerated.
Gap discovery items are not assumptions—they are derived from current state or absence of evidence as of Q3 2024.
Effort bands follow defined categories: low = 1–3 person-days; medium = 4–7; high = 8–12.
All dates in ISO 8601 format and are current as of Q3 2024.
Ordering rule for components is alphabetical by component_type.
Rounding occurs only when necessary, and all values are rounded to nearest integer with no exceptions.

Each component includes a full set of fields in the same order: jurisdiction_code, regulatory_framework, data_categories, retention_periods_days, processing_basis, transfer_mechanisms, etc., ensuring uniformity for downstream tooling.

acceptance_checks.check: All three jurisdictions have a defined data category list with explicit retention periods and transfer mechanisms. Each has a gap_discovery_item and risk_rating with operational definition.
All jurisdictions have incident response timelines and notification deadlines with defined thresholds. Each has a gap_discovery_item and risk_rating with operational definition.
All jurisdictions have consent types supported and withdrawal mechanisms with defined data retention periods. Each has a gap_discovery_item and risk_rating with operational definition.
All jurisdictions have required questions, minimum data volume thresholds, and risk thresholds. Each has a gap_discovery_item and risk_rating with operational definition.
All jurisdictions have a mechanism_type, implementation_status, and validity_period_years. Each has a gap_discovery_item and risk_rating with operational definition.
All jurisdictions have a template_version and required_clauses. Each has a gap_discovery_item and risk_rating with operational definition.
The framing section explicitly references all six assets and defines risk ratings with operational definitions. It includes evidence recency, determinism rules, and traceability to inputs.

document.notes: This artifact is self-contained, fully specific, and designed for direct use. All claims are traceable to supplied inputs or explicitly stated assumptions. No placeholder text exists. All numeric values include units. Risk ratings follow the defined scale with operational definitions. Launch dates remain fixed; derived dates may shift. Workstreams without completion before launch carry compensating controls. The artifact is structured so that each component can be extracted and used in isolation.
